intro:
Use it to ask for a sentence: what went wrong, what to fix first, why somebody gave the score they did. It is a dialog whose body is a place to write, with Cancel and Submit in the band around it.

`Submit` cannot be pressed while the field is empty, and it does not close the dialog. You close it once the message has been sent, so a send that fails still has somewhere to say so.

For a yes-or-no confirmation use a plain dialog. For a form with several fields, build the form.
usage:
<Feedback>
  <Feedback.Trigger>Send feedback</Feedback.Trigger>
  <Feedback.Content>
    <Feedback.Panel>
      <Feedback.Title>What should we fix first?</Feedback.Title>
      <Feedback.Close />
      <Feedback.Field placeholder="Tell us what got in your way" />
    </Feedback.Panel>
    <Feedback.Footer>
      <Feedback.Cancel />
      <Feedback.Submit onSubmit={(message) => send(message)} />
    </Feedback.Footer>
  </Feedback.Content>
</Feedback>

parts.Trigger: What opens the dialog. A plain button, or your own through `render`.
parts.Content: The shell: the darker band and everything set in it. `inline` draws it in the page instead of over it.
parts.Panel: The well. The title, the close button and the field go here, along with anything else the question needs.
parts.Title: The question. In a dialog it is also the dialog's accessible name.
parts.Close: The ✕ in the corner of the panel.
parts.Field: The text area. It has no border of its own, because it is already inside a well.
parts.Footer: The row the two actions sit in.
parts.Cancel: Closes the dialog. Call `preventDefault` in `onClick` to do something else, such as going back a step.
parts.Submit: Calls `onSubmit` with the message. Disabled while the field is empty unless you pass `disabled` yourself.

examples.title: In a dialog
examples.description: The usual shape. `Feedback.Trigger` opens it, and `render` makes your own button the trigger. Hold `open` yourself so you can close the dialog when the message has gone.

examples.title: A send that fails
examples.description: Because `Submit` leaves the dialog open, a failed request can say so in the panel, with the message still in the field. This demo fails the first time and succeeds on the retry.

examples.title: Tags over the field
examples.description: Anything can go in the panel above the field. Here a tag is enough to send on its own, so `Submit` is given its own `disabled` and the field becomes optional.

examples.title: Score first, words second
examples.description: Two steps in one dialog. Asking for the score first gives the sentence something to be about. Back is a `Feedback.Cancel` whose `onClick` calls `preventDefault`, which stops it closing.

examples.title: Keeping a draft
examples.description: Pass `value` and `onValueChange` to hold the message yourself. It survives the dialog being closed, and you can check it as it is typed. This one needs twenty characters before it can be sent.

notes:
### In the page

`<Feedback.Content inline>` draws the same shell in the page, with no backdrop and nothing to open. Cancel and the close button have nothing to close there, so they only call `onOpenChange(false)`. Use that to clear the field or to hide the box.

### Closing

A click outside the dialog or the Escape key closes it. Pass `dismissible={false}` to `Feedback` to turn both off, for a message that a stray click should not throw away. Cancel and the close button still work.

### Keyboard

Enter adds a new line. Command+Enter on a Mac, or Control+Enter elsewhere, sends the message, as long as `Submit` is enabled. Focus is kept inside the dialog while it is open and returns to the trigger when it closes.

### The empty state

While `Submit` is disabled it drops its fill, where most buttons would only dim. A dimmed accent button still looks like the one to press. Pass `disabled` to decide for yourself when the message can be sent: `disabled={false}` allows an empty one.

### What it is built on

The dialog is the Base UI dialog, which the package depends on directly. It does not use your project's own dialog component, so it looks the same whichever one you have.
